title: Author Correction Selective manipulation of the inositol metabolic pathway for induction of salt-tolerance in indica ric

predicted_errors.error_location: Results, 'Analysis of homozygous transgenic lines' (growth parameters) vs. Figure 3 caption
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The text states 'Comparative shoot-length, root-length and fresh wt. taken after 10 days-stress indicated 7PcINO1-line, 10PcIMT1-line and 6DC1-line as the best in terms of growth parameters (Fig. 3a–c)', but the caption of the same figure reads 'Comparative phenotypic study for shoot-length, root-length and fresh-weight of transgenics with untransformed lines under variable NaCl stresses kept for 7 days'. The stress duration for the data in Fig. 3 is reported inconsistently (7 vs 10 days).

predicted_errors.error_location: Results, 'Construction of expression vectors...' paragraph (Supplementary Fig. S5g–m)
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The same supplementary panels are cited for two distinct datasets in consecutive sentences: 'Among the T₀ putative transgenics (Supplementary Fig. S5g–m) hptII gene specific PCR positive plants were selected...' and 'Homozygous T₂ lines showing the presence of hptII gene at 1 kb, PcINO1 gene at 1.5 kb and PcIMT1 gene at 1.1 kb region respectively (Supplementary Fig. S5g–m)'. The same figure panels cannot simultaneously depict T₀ putative transgenic screening and T₂ homozygous line genotyping; one of the citations is incorrect.

predicted_errors.error_location: Results, generation/selection of transgenic lines (T₂/T₃ segregation)
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: Lines are declared 'Homozygous T₂ lines' and used for Southern analysis, yet segregation analysis — the very assay used to establish single-locus inheritance and homozygosity — is reported only afterwards on 'Southern positive T₃ PcINO1-plants ... were used for segregation analysis (Supplementary Tables S4a–S6a)'. Homozygosity cannot be asserted at T₂ before the segregation data were obtained; the generation/sequence of steps is internally inconsistent (also with the Abstract, which refers to 'Homozygous T₃/T₄ transgenic plants').

predicted_errors.error_location: Figure 1 caption (b) and corresponding Results text
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The text states that only 'Two candidate genes viz. PcINO1 and PcIMT1, earlier isolated from Porteresia coarctata' were cloned, yet the construct is named 'pCAMBIA1301-PcINO1/OsINO1 construct containing PcINO1/OsINO1 gene' in both the text and the Fig. 1b caption. An OsINO1 (endogenous rice MIPS) construct is never described, characterized, or analysed anywhere in the study, so the construct designation contradicts the reported experimental design.

predicted_errors.error_location: Abstract vs. Results (recovery after stress withdrawal)
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The Abstract claims 'The PcIMT1-lines or the double transgenic lines (DC1) ... were less efficient in such respect', whereas the Results state 'Even after 300 mM salt stress for 10 days, 7PcINO1-line, 10PcIMT1-line and 6DC1-line fully recovered their normal physiological activity' and 'recovery of chlorophyll content in all transgenic lines'. The reported recovery data do not distinguish PcINO1 lines as superior and thus conflict with the Abstract's conclusion.

The paper states PcIMT1 is 'the inositol methyl transferase gene (PcIMT1) producing pinitol in planta'. Myo-inositol O-methyltransferase converts myo-inositol to D-ononitol; conversion of ononitol to D-pinitol requires a separate ononitol epimerase. Attributing direct pinitol synthesis to IMT1 misstates the enzymatic step and overstates what the transgene alone can do.

'Data represented average of three plants ± SD (P ≤ 0.05)' attaches a significance threshold to descriptive error bars without naming any statistical test, specifying what comparison was significant, or reporting test statistics; with n = 3 plants this is an uninterpretable statistical statement.
